articles.title: Addisu Gobena smashes Sydney Marathon record as Jepchirchir wins fourth women’s major
articles.summary: Ethiopian former javelin thrower claims men’s race in 2hr 4min 42sec. Kenyan adds harbourside crown to Boston, New York and London titles. Ethiopia’s Addisu Gobena surged to a record-breaking victory in the men’s race at the Sydney Marathon, while Kenya’s Peres Jepchirchir claimed the women’s crown…
body: In perfect conditions, Gobena won the hotly contested men’s race in two hours four minutes and 42 seconds – more than a minute and a half quicker than the previous record on the hilly harbourside course which attracted 40,000 competitors from around the world.

The 21-year-old Ethiopian, who was a javelin thrower until 2023, broke away with compatriot Chimdessa Debele Gudeta from the lead pack of six runners inside the final two kilometres and then surged ahead on the downhill finish to the Sydney Opera House to win by four seconds.

Gobena, who finished second behind Hailemaryam Kiros last year, celebrated by punching the air after crossing the finish line. “I am very happy. Last year I came second, I learned from my mistake, and I went back home and I worked on my mistake to perform and break the record today,” said Gobena through an interpreter.
Lesotho’s Tebello Ramakongoana was third in 2:04:57. The top seven finishers, including Kiros, were all inside Kiros’ record time of 2:06:06 set in last year’s race.

articles.title: William Jewell running back MicahJo Barnett dies after medical emergency during game
articles.summary: Junior taken to hospital after first-quarter emergency. Division II season opener suspended and later canceled. School plans vigil for Barnett and his family. William Jewell College running back MicahJo Barnett had a medical emergency on the sideline during ⁠the school’s season opener on Saturday.
body: Barnett, a junior, ⁠reportedly experienced seizure-like ⁠symptoms during ​the first quarter of the Division II contest against Fort Lewis College. The game was played ⁠on William Jewell’s campus in Liberty, Missouri, about 20 miles northeast of Kansas City.
Barnett experienced the emergency at ⁠approximately 12.20pm local time. Paramedics from the Liberty Fire Department ​took him to a ‌local hospital, where he was ‌pronounced dead.
Officials planned a vigil Saturday night on the school’s quad to honor Barnett and his family.

Barnett rushed six times for 29 yards during the game, which included a one-yard touchdown run at ⁠the 5:15 mark of the first quarter for the ​game’s lone score. The ​game was halted with ​4:32 left in the first.

articles.title: Itauma punches himself out against Hrgovic in world-title fight
articles.summary: Filip Hrgovic shatters Moses Itauma's world-title dream as the Briton appears to punch himself out in an extraordinary heavyweight world-title contest in London.
body: Filip Hrgovic ripped up the script and shattered Moses Itauma's world-title dream as the Briton appeared to punch himself out in an extraordinary heavyweight contest in London.
Itauma, 21, controlled most of the fight and scored a second-round knockdown but faded as his relentless output caught up with him.
Hrgovic weathered the storm and piled on the pressure in the ninth. With Itauma barely able to stand, his legs unsteady and body swaying before slumping in the corner, his team threw in the towel.

Itauma - who needed medical attention before leaving the arena on a stretcher - had been a heavy favourite after tearing through his first 14 opponents and was spoken about as heavyweight boxing's next superstar.

articles.title: Filip Hrgovic stuns Britain’s Moses Itauma to claim IBF world heavyweight title
articles.summary: 21-year-old Itauma stopped after ninth-round rally. 34-year-old Hrgovic is first Croat to win such a title. Moses Itauma’s hopes of becoming the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in history lay in ruins after the extraordinarily tough and resilient Filip Hrgovic stopped him in the ninth…
body: The fight changed course when Itauma’s stamina suddenly dipped and he began to weave in woozy fatigue as Hrgovic fought back with granite-like determination. Itauma could not withstand the dark storm rolling over him in the ninth and he sank back against the ropes as Hrgovic opened up with renewed conviction. Just as the referee stepped in to stop the fight, Ben Davison, Itauma’s trainer, also sent a white towel sailing sadly over the listing ropes to save his man from a knockout.

The shocking twist was too much for the 21-year-old and he left the ring on a stretcher, apparently having injured his knee. But the damage was done by the remarkable fightback from his opponent, who made his own significant slice of boxing history. The admirable Hrgovic is the first world heavyweight champion from Croatia – a country that has no real boxing heritage.

articles.title: Novak Djokovic feels ‘as best as I can be’ before tilt at 25th grand slam title in New York
articles.summary: Serb hopes to take advantage of wide-open men’s draw. Elena Rybakina has eyes on No 1 world ranking. Novak Djokovic said he was as prepared as he could be for the US Open as he attempts to take advantage of the wide-open men’s draw and battle for a potential 25th grand slam title.
body: Djokovic arrived in New York having competed only once after his semi-final run at Wimbledon, losing in his opening match of the Cincinnati Open to Thiago Agustín Tirante while struggling with the humidity. However, he now sees the silver lining in that defeat, which he believes gave him the time to make sure he was in optimal shape for the US Open. “I don’t like early losses anywhere, to be honest, but it gave me time to be prepared for US Open in a most adequate way,” he said. “I had almost a few weeks, actually two weeks, to really train and get my body and mind into the right state, prepared for what’s coming up.
“So it remains to be seen. If you ask me if I’m prepared, I feel like I am as best as I can be, but it’s different training and then getting out on the Arthur Ashe Stadium and playing best-of-five.”

Over the course of the past two years, nobody other than Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner has been as consistent at the grand slams as Djokovic, who has reached the semi-finals or better in six of his last seven such tournaments. However, Sinner and Alcaraz account for five of those defeats, along with a retirement loss at the Australian Open last year.

articles.title: Messi's fantastic four as rampant Miami snap winless streak
articles.summary: Lionel Messi scored four goals as Inter Miami snapped their five-game winless streak with a 7-1 thrashing of struggling Montreal in Major League Soccer on Saturday. Miami have endured a rocky spell since the resumption of play following the World Cup finals, losing four of their previous five games…
body: But the reigning MLS Cup champions got back to winning ways with a confident performance against Montreal, who are languishing second from bottom in the Eastern Conference.
Brazil international Casemiro, who joined Miami after the World Cup, bagged his first goal for the champions with a 20th minute header at the Nu Stadium.
Montreal though hit back with a 37th-minute goal from Fabian Herbers, the German midfielder's low shot from the edge of the area squeezing into the bottom corner.
But Miami did not have to wait long to regain the lead, and went 2-1 up when a low curling free-kick from Messi somehow bamboozled Montreal goalkeeper Thomas Gillier in the 40th minute.

articles.title: Cameron beats Mayer to become unified light-middleweight champion
articles.summary: Chantelle Cameron produced one of the finest displays of her career to beat Mikaela Mayer and add the WBA and WBC light-middleweight titles to her WBO belt.
body: An engrossing encounter was narrowly won by the British fighter by unanimous decision - 97-93 on two scorecards and 96-94 on the other.
American Mayer disagreed with the decision, claiming she "outboxed" Cameron – leading to an angry exchange of words in the ring.
The possibility of a rematch was also floated, with Mayer suggesting Cameron had benefited from home advantage – to the champion's chagrin, as she said "talk is cheap".
It means Cameron remains unbeaten since her second fight with Katie Taylor in 2023, and with 23 victories in 24 professional encounters.

articles.title: Fery's dreams of maiden ATP Tour title ended in Winston-Salem Open final
articles.summary: Arthur Fery's hopes of landing his maiden ATP Tour title at Winston-Salem Open was ended in emphatic fashion by Peruvian Ignacio Buse on Saturday.
body: From 3-3 in the first set, Fery lost six straight games before eventually going down 6-3 6-2 to Buse.
The promising 22-year-old clinched his second trophy of the season having lifted his maiden tour-level trophy at the ATP 500 event in Hamburg.
Fery was aiming to add to his already memorable season having reached the semi-finals at Wimbledon and he is set for a new career high Monday.
With his spot in the Winston-Salem final, 24-year-old Fery has moved up to a new career high of No 33 in the live rankings, overtaking Cameron Norrie as the British No 1 in doing so.

articles.title: Game 2 Gamethread: Giants vs. Diamondbacks
articles.summary: Well, they lost the first one. But they’re back to try it again! The San Francisco Giants are hosting the Arizona Diamondbacks for the second game of a doubleheader, and are hoping to split the four-game series.
body: It’s an exciting pitching situation for the Giants, as right-hander Yunior Marte takes the mound for his MLB debut. Marte — not to be confused with the reliever of the same name, who pitched for San Francisco in 2022 — is a young prospect whom the Giants acquired a year ago in the Mike Yastrzemski trade. He is, shockingly, following in Jonah Cox’s footsteps as the second player the Giants have called up directly from AA this year … after going nearly a decade without making such a move.

For Arizona, it’s lefty Mitch Bratt, who is also a 23-year old lefty. Bratt, who was a fifth-round pick in 2021, has made nine appearances in his debut season, and is 1-2 with a 4.54 ERA, a 5.28 FIP, and 28 strikeouts against 25 walks in 39.2 innings. After a pair of great starts to open the month, Bratt has given up three runs in three innings in each of his last two games.

articles.title: Hovland leads Scheffler in FedExCup thriller as McIlroy makes late push
articles.summary: Viktor Hovland takes a one-shot lead into the final round of the Tour Championship, as Scottie Scheffler stayed in contention and Rory McIlroy kept his FedExCup hopes alive.
body: Hovland produced a birdie-birdie finish to post a five-under 65 at East Lake, lifting the 2023 FedExCup champion to 15 under and with a narrow advantage over playing partner Ryan Gerard.

The halfway co-leaders were chased down by a star-studded chasing pack during a thrilling Saturday at the PGA Tour's season finale, with world no 1 Scottie Scheffler three shots back in third spot and chasing a second FedExCup title.

Scheffler is joined on 12 under by Chris Gotterup, Adam Scott and Ludvig Åberg, who produced a three-birdie finish to his third-round 65, as McIlroy jumped to tied-seventh after setting the early clubhouse target with a round-of-the-day 63.
McIlroy sits five strokes back alongside Cameron Young as he searches for a record-extending fourth FedExCup title, with all 29 players in the field under-par heading into the final round.

articles.title: Europe's hopes fade at FM Championship as Maguire impresses in Ireland
articles.summary: Ruoning Yin produced a final-hole chip-in to take a one-shot lead into the final round of the LPGA Tour’s FM Championship, as European title hopes faded in Boston.
body: Yin holed her chip from just off the 18th green, having also posted a 20-foot birdie on the par-three 16th, to close a four-under 68 and move to 12 under at TPC Boston.
The five-time LPGA Tour winner holds a slender lead over South Korean duo Sei Young Kim and Hyo Joo Kim, with Somi Lee a further three strokes back alongside American Jenny Bae.

"I think my swing is in a good spot, my putting and every part of my game I think are pretty good," Yin said. "I'm just going to play my game. I'm not going to play safe when it's time to go aggressive."

This week's event is the last LPGA Tour tournament before the Solheim Cup, live on Sky Sports from September 11-13, with Team USA trio Lauren Coughlin, Allisen Corpuz and Lindy Duncan all heading into the final day on seven under.
